newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan-run Kazakh field to begin output in April.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan-run Kazakh field to begin output in April.

text.p: Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp said on Thursday its joint oil exploration project in Kazakhstan's northwestern Caspian Sea area would start producing crude oil in April.
"The Kazakh oil field will start production in April and it will reach maximum capacity within one year," a company official told Reuters by telephone.
He said the maximum daily capacity would be between 20,000 to 30,000 barrels per day.
Chinese Petroleum took over the management of the oil field, which has recoverable oil reserves of about 90 million barrels, from Kazakhstan state-run oil company in April 1996.
Chinese Petroleum holds the right to extract the oil field for 25 years and may extend for another 25 years.
The state monopoly did not expect to ship any oil extracted from the Kazakh field, because the project's marketing will be handled by a Houston-based U.S. company, the official said.
Chinese Petroleum invested about US$14 million in the US$40 million joint project. Several unidentified foreign companies from Israel and the United States also took part in the deal.
The Kazakh oil project is part of Chinese Petroleum's strategy to shift its oil exploration from exploring new oil fields to acquiring other oil companies' proven fields.
